The statement’s 75 bp hike to 3.75–4% and ongoing balance-sheet reduction reflect a restrictive, Taylor-rule–type reaction to elevated inflation, consistent with the modern practice of targeting the policy rate (Goodfriend) and DSGE-guided emphasis on expectations. Acknowledging cumulative tightening and policy lags aligns with Rudebusch-style dynamics and the literature on imperfect information, suggesting some gradualism in the pace of future hikes. Yet the emphasis on broad price pressures and war-related supply shocks—where optimal policy typically only partially accommodates—keeps the overall communication hawkish, even as data dependence tempers the tone. Net takeaway: restrictive with a cautious tilt.
